vocabulary.meaning_en: an amount taken off a price; to reduce a price
vocabulary.example: They discounted all the shoes by 20%.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a time when things are sold at lower prices
vocabulary.note_ar: on sale = عليه تخفيض (في بريطانيا قد تعني معروض للبيع فقط)، for sale = معروض للبيع
vocabulary.example: The big summer sale starts on Monday.
vocabulary.note_en: on sale = at a lower price (in Britain it can also mean just available to buy); for sale = available to buy.

vocabulary.meaning_en: something bought cheaply for its value
vocabulary.example: This sofa was a real bargain.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a product sold at a special low price
vocabulary.example: Pasta is on special offer this week.

vocabulary.meaning_en: selling old stock cheaply to make space for new goods
vocabulary.example: Everything in the clearance sale is half price.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a paper or code that gives you money off
vocabulary.example: Use this coupon to get 20% off.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a prepaid paper you can use instead of money
vocabulary.example: I got a $50 gift voucher for my birthday.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a special offer to make people buy something; a higher job
vocabulary.example: The shop is running a promotion on phones.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a good price; an agreement
vocabulary.example: I found some great deals online.

vocabulary.meaning_en: for 50% of the normal price
vocabulary.example: All jackets are half price today.

vocabulary.meaning_en: made lower in price
vocabulary.example: These shirts are reduced from $40 to $25.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an amount out of a hundred
vocabulary.example: What percentage of the price can I save?

vocabulary.meaning_en: to spend less money
vocabulary.example: You save $10 if you buy two.

vocabulary.meaning_en: buy one item and get a second one free
vocabulary.meaning_ar: اشترِ واحدة واحصل على الثانية مجاناً
vocabulary.note_ar: BOGO اختصار من أول حرف في كل كلمة
vocabulary.example: There's a BOGO offer on T-shirts.
vocabulary.note_en: BOGO is made from the first letter of each word.

vocabulary.meaning_en: only for a short period
vocabulary.example: This price is for a limited time only.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a sale at a certain season, like summer or winter
vocabulary.example: I always wait for the seasonal sales.
vocabulary.note_en: season = a time of year; seasonal = related to a season.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the big sale day after Thanksgiving in the USA
vocabulary.example: Shops are very crowded on Black Friday.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the time when a season finishes
vocabulary.example: End-of-season prices are very low.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a shop that sells a brand's goods cheaply
vocabulary.note_ar: أصلها factory outlet = منفذ بيع المصنع
vocabulary.example: I bought these trainers at the outlet.
vocabulary.note_en: Originally "factory outlet" = a shop where a factory sells its own goods.

vocabulary.meaning_en: in large amounts
vocabulary.example: It's cheaper to buy rice in bulk.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to come to an end; to stop being valid
vocabulary.example: The offer expires on Sunday.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the rail with cheap old stock in a shop
vocabulary.example: I found this dress on the clearance rack.
vocabulary.note_en: rack = a stand or frame for hanging or holding things.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a lasting cut in a product's original price
vocabulary.example: There's a big markdown on winter coats.

vocabulary.meaning_en: being a member of a club or group
vocabulary.example: Membership gives you free delivery.

vocabulary.meaning_en: money you get back after buying something
vocabulary.example: I got 10% cashback on my order.

vocabulary.meaning_en: at a price you can pay
vocabulary.note_ar: من afford = يقدر مالياً؛ ليست بالضرورة cheap
vocabulary.example: We're looking for an affordable flat.
vocabulary.note_en: From "afford" (to have enough money for something); it doesn't always mean cheap.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a label showing the price
vocabulary.example: Check the price tag before you buy.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a large group of people
vocabulary.example: The crowd was wild.

vocabulary.meaning_en: out of control; living in nature
vocabulary.example: The fans went wild after the goal.
vocabulary.note_en: wild animals = animals that live in nature, not with people.

vocabulary.meaning_en: liking new and exciting things
vocabulary.note_ar: adventure + ous؛ اللاحقة ous تحوّل الاسم إلى صفة (humour → humorous)
vocabulary.example: She's adventurous and loves travelling alone.
vocabulary.note_en: adventure + ous; the ending -ous turns a noun into an adjective (humour → humorous).

vocabulary.meaning_en: a card that collects points when you shop
vocabulary.example: Do you have a loyalty card?

vocabulary.meaning_en: something done to fool someone; to fool
vocabulary.example: Some bargains are just tricks.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to suddenly fall down
vocabulary.example: She collapsed onto the sofa, tired.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to stay alive through something difficult
vocabulary.example: I can't survive another week like this!

vocabulary.meaning_en: a place where a battle is fought
vocabulary.example: The shop looked like a battlefield.
vocabulary.note_en: battle (a fight between armies) + field (an open area).

vocabulary.meaning_en: at the same time
vocabulary.example: Meanwhile, James was restocking the shelves.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to breathe out loudly because you are tired or sad
vocabulary.example: He sighed and closed the book.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to fill shelves with goods again
vocabulary.example: They restock the shelves every morning.
vocabulary.note_en: re (again) + stock: fill the shelves again.

vocabulary.meaning_en: very silly or crazy behaviour
vocabulary.example: Every year it's the same madness.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to speak quietly, often in an unhappy way
vocabulary.example: He muttered something about the prices.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to promise strongly
vocabulary.example: She swore she would never be late again.

fine_lines.title: coupon vs voucher
fine_lines.explanation_ar: coupon يقلّل السعر: يعطيك خصماً بنسبة أو مبلغ، لكنك تظل تدفع. voucher نفسه يُعتبر نقوداً مدفوعة مسبقاً بقيمة معينة، فتشتري به بدون دفع حتى قيمته. باختصار: الكوبون يخفض السعر، والفاوتشر يدفع السعر.

examples.sentence: With this coupon, you get 20% off your next order.
I paid for the book with a $20 gift voucher.

fine_lines.explanation_en: A coupon lowers the price: it gives you a discount (a percentage or an amount), but you still pay. A voucher is like prepaid money with a set value, so you can buy with it without paying, up to its value. In short: a coupon cuts the price; a voucher pays the price.

fine_lines.title: discount vs markdown
fine_lines.explanation_ar: discount مصطلح عام لأي تقليل في السعر، وقد يكون مؤقتاً (عرض، كوبون) ثم يعود السعر الأصلي. markdown تخفيض دائم للسعر الأصلي لأن المنتج لم يُبع أو لأن الموسم انتهى، وغالباً لا يرتفع السعر مرة أخرى بل قد ينخفض أكثر.

examples.sentence: Members get a 10% discount this weekend only.
The jacket didn't sell, so there was a markdown from $100 to $60.

fine_lines.explanation_en: "Discount" is a general word for any price cut, and it can be temporary (an offer, a coupon) before the original price returns. A markdown is a permanent cut to the original price because the item didn't sell or the season ended; the price usually doesn't go back up and may drop even more.

fine_lines.title: on sale vs for sale
fine_lines.explanation_ar: for sale تعني أن الشيء معروض للبيع فقط. on sale تعني في أمريكا أن عليه تخفيضاً، لكن في بريطانيا قد تعني فقط أنه متاح للبيع مثل for sale.

examples.sentence: These boots are on sale; they're 30% off.

fine_lines.explanation_en: "For sale" means something is available to buy. In the US, "on sale" means it has a lower price, but in Britain it can simply mean it's available to buy, like "for sale".

fine_lines.title: affordable vs cheap
fine_lines.explanation_ar: cheap تعني رخيص. affordable تعني سعره معقول وتقدر عليه، وهي نسبية تختلف من شخص لآخر، ولا تعني بالضرورة أن الشيء رخيص.

examples.sentence: These plastic cups are very cheap.
The new phone is expensive, but it's affordable for me.

fine_lines.explanation_en: "Cheap" means low in price. "Affordable" means the price is reasonable and you can pay it; it depends on the person and doesn't always mean cheap.

fine_lines.title: as vs like (role vs similarity)
fine_lines.explanation_ar: as تبيّن الدور الحقيقي (مثل الكاف في العربية بمعنى «بصفته»): works as a teacher يعني هو مدرس فعلاً. like للتشبيه: works like a teacher يعني يتصرف مثل المدرسين لكنه ليس مدرساً.

examples.sentence: He works as a teacher in a small school.
He explains things like a teacher, but he's an engineer.

fine_lines.explanation_en: "As" shows a real role: "works as a teacher" means he really is a teacher. "Like" shows similarity: "works like a teacher" means he behaves like a teacher but isn't one.

fine_lines.title: pay through the nose vs rip-off
fine_lines.explanation_ar: rip-off يعني أن هناك خداعاً أو استغلالاً في السعر. pay through the nose يعني أنك دفعت مبلغاً باهظاً جداً، وقد تكون تعرف أنه مبالغ فيه دون أن يخدعك أحد، مثل تذاكر مباراة مهمة.

examples.sentence: We paid through the nose for the final match tickets.
That taxi fare was a total rip-off.

fine_lines.explanation_en: A rip-off means you were cheated or charged unfairly. "Pay through the nose" means you paid a very high price; you may know it's too much without anyone cheating you, like tickets for a big match.

expressions.meaning_ar: يدفع مبلغاً باهظاً / يدفع دم قلبه
expressions.example: I paid through the nose for this ticket.
expressions.meaning_en: pay a very high price for something

expressions.phrase: cost an arm and a leg
expressions.example: Their wedding cost an arm and a leg.
Sara, dramatic as ever, collapsed on the sofa.
expressions.meaning_en: as usual ("as ever" is more literary)

expressions.example: I found a jacket at a huge discount.
expressions.meaning_en: with a very big price cut

expressions.example: By the end of the day, I was exhausted.
expressions.meaning_en: finally, after something has happened gradually

expressions.example: At least the promotions keep the store alive.
expressions.meaning_en: keep the shop open and in business

grammar.title: Three uses of "as"
grammar.explanation_ar: 1) as بمعنى while (بينما / أثناء). 2) as بمعنى because أو since (بما أن / لأن)، وغالباً في بداية الجملة. 3) as لبيان الدور (كـ / بصفته)، ولا نستخدم like هنا لأنها للتشبيه.
examples: James sighed as he restocked the sale section.
As it was Black Friday, the mall was crowded.
grammar.explanation_en: 1) "As" can mean "while" (at the same time). 2) "As" can mean "because" or "since", often at the start of a sentence. 3) "As" can show a role (in the job or position of); we don't use "like" here because "like" is for similarity.

grammar.title: Reported yes/no questions with if / whether
grammar.explanation_ar: الأسئلة التي إجابتها نعم أو لا (Do you...? Is this...?) ننقلها باستخدام if أو whether (بمعنى «إذا / هل»)، ثم الفاعل والفعل بدون فعل مساعد للسؤال، مع الحفاظ على الماضي وتغيير this إلى that منطقياً. انتبه: whether (سواء / إذا) تختلف عن weather (الطقس).
examples: "Do you have a loyalty card?" → The seller asked if I had a loyalty card.
"Is this shirt affordable?" → Omar asked whether that shirt was affordable.
grammar.explanation_en: Yes/no questions (Do you...? Is this...?) are reported with "if" or "whether", followed by subject + verb with no question auxiliary. Keep the past tense and change "this" to "that" where it makes sense. Careful: "whether" is different from "weather".

grammar.title: No "the" with general plural nouns
grammar.explanation_ar: عندما نتكلم عن شيء بشكل عام بصيغة الجمع لا نستخدم the، عكس العربية. نستخدم the فقط عندما نحدد أشياء معينة.
examples: The books on the table are mine.
grammar.explanation_en: When we talk about things in general using a plural noun, we don't use "the". We use "the" only for specific things.

questions.question: A prepaid paper you can use instead of money is a:
questions.explanation_ar: voucher قيمته مدفوعة مسبقاً ويُستخدم كنقود، أما coupon فيخفض السعر فقط.
questions.explanation_en: A voucher is prepaid and works like money; a coupon only lowers the price.

questions.question: He works ___ a teacher at a primary school.
questions.explanation_ar: as لبيان الدور الحقيقي، و like للتشبيه.
questions.explanation_en: "As" shows a real role; "like" shows similarity.

questions.question: "Do you have a loyalty card?" → The seller asked ___ I had a loyalty card.
questions.explanation_ar: أسئلة نعم/لا ننقلها بـ if أو whether.
questions.explanation_en: Yes/no questions are reported with "if" or "whether".

questions.question: The jacket didn't sell, so the shop cut its original price for good. This is a:
questions.explanation_ar: markdown تخفيض دائم للسعر الأصلي لأن المنتج لم يُبع.
questions.explanation_en: A markdown is a permanent cut to the original price because the item didn't sell.

questions.question: ___ it was Black Friday, the mall was very crowded.
We paid ___ for the final match tickets. They were extremely expensive.
questions.explanation_ar: pay through the nose = يدفع مبلغاً باهظاً.
questions.explanation_en: pay through the nose = pay a very high price.

questions.question: "Affordable" means:
choices: at a price you can pay
questions.explanation_ar: affordable = بسعر معقول تقدر عليه، وليس بالضرورة رخيصاً.
questions.explanation_en: Affordable = a reasonable price you can pay, not always cheap.

Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation_ar: عند الكلام العام عن جمع لا نستخدم the.
questions.explanation_en: When talking about plural things in general, we don't use "the".
